Subject: Transient egress grace period & subprocessor roster for regional failover

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the last call. As DataCo's DPO I need to confirm two items before we proceed with the pilot:

1) Can you confirm the maximum transient egress window when a regional pin (EU/APAC/US) fails over for maintenance or capacity reasons? We need an upper bound (minutes) and whether you provide an SLA exception notification.

2) For any cross-border transient routing, please provide the full roster of subprocessors that could process DataCo traffic during that window (include cloud regions, CDN providers, logging/monitoring vendors). A CSV is fine.

We'd also like to see the DPA clause you'd rely on for transient routing + suggested addendum language so our contracting team can review.

Attached: DataCo_DPO_Roster_Request.pdf (summary of the questions).

Can you loop in legal and infra contacts? We prefer to keep this scoped to factual answers rather than negotiations at this stage.

Best,
Elena

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Rishi (AM), Markus (infra), Marissa (acct lead) and Laura (legal) so we can answer cleanly.

Short answers up front:
- Max transient egress window we allow for planned maintenance or immediate capacity failover: 30 minutes per failover event. Typical windows are 2–8 minutes for automated failovers; 30 minutes is the contractual backstop for unplanned/manual operations.
- SLA: we provide proactive notifications (email + webhook) for planned maintenance. For spontaneous failovers we emit an event in the incident stream and provide a follow-up within 24 hours summarizing affected regions and routing.
- Subprocessors: we can provide a current roster (CSV) listing cloud regions and third-party services that may briefly touch data during failover. See attached redwood-subprocessors-20260720.csv — it marks which subprocessors are used in transient routing vs. persistent storage.

Next steps: Markus will provide the infra/security detail (encryption-in-transit, key usage, logs), and Laura will propose a short DPA addendum we can share. Rishi and Marissa — can you confirm commercial implications for the pilot?

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi

Hi Elena / team — technical details from infra: please see inline.

On Wed, Jul 15, 2026 at 09:47 PDT Irene Choi wrote:
> Short answers up front:
> - Max transient egress window we allow for planned maintenance or immediate capacity failover: 30 minutes per failover event.

Operational detail:
- Typical behavior: automatic region-affinity routing will attempt local serving in the pinned region. If capacity < threshold, we fail traffic to the next-best region according to routing policy (priority: same-country region -> same-continent -> nearest region). Automated failover takes ~2–8 minutes (DNS + runtime reconnection + cache repopulation).
- Contractual backstop: we accept up to 30 minutes where traffic may be routed outside the pinned region; we log each event and provide timestamps (start/end) per request.

Security controls during the window:
- Encryption: all in-transit traffic uses TLS1.3 with mutual auth for internal service-to-service; customer payloads are never stored unencrypted outside pinned region — transient KV caches are encrypted with server-side keys and evicted on failback.
- Keys: No export of customer-managed KMS keys; by default we use Redwood-managed keys unless the customer supplies a Bring-Your-Own-Key configuration. If BYOK is used, the key material never leaves the customer-controlled key store.
- Logging & audit: we generate a per-request routing log with timestamps, source region, destination region, and subprocessor IDs. These logs are available in the audit exports (S3 or streamed to your SIEM) and we can provide a 30-day slice for review.

Subprocessors relevant to transient routing (excerpt):
- Global edge: FastEdge CDN (edge PoPs) — may act as TCP termination during extreme bursts (no payload persistence).
- Transit/Network: Acme Transit Services (regional backbone) — for expedited routing between regions during failover.
- Monitoring: SysWatch Monitoring (metrics + traces).
- Persistent storage is never moved to a different legal region without explicit data residency configuration.

I'll attach the CSV with tags: transient/persistent and region column.

-Markus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus — useful detail. A couple follow-ups: 

1) For the 30-minute backstop, is there an objective threshold (error rate / capacity %) that triggers a manual escalation or is it purely human-determined? We'd like objective triggers to include in our addendum.

2) For FastEdge CDN: does it ever decrypt payloads in the edge PoP, or is it strictly TCP/TLS termination? If decryption happens, we need the vendor contract and location of PoPs used for AtlasCommerce traffic.

3) Please provide a redacted sample of the routing audit log (one event) and a short extract of the CSV showing APAC-related subprocessors.

Attached: contracting@atlascommerce.com will expect a short DPA addendum draft as Word track-changes. Also include any SOC2 control ID references for routing and network security.

Regards,
Elena
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Márquez <dpo@dataco.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient egress grace period & subprocessor roster for regional failover

Elena — thanks for the specificity, I appreciate it. Draft proposed addendum language below (track changes version attached):

- For planned maintenance, Redwood will provide no less than 72 hours' notice and a targeted time window.
- For automated or manual failovers, Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to keep cross-region routing to under 30 minutes per failover event; automatic remediation typically completes in 2–8 minutes.
- Objective trigger for escalation: if pinned-region availability drops below 85% over a rolling 5-minute window OR error rate for pinned-region requests increases by >300% vs. baseline, Redwood will declare a region failover incident and notify the customer.
- Subprocessors that may briefly process traffic during a failover are listed in the attached CSV; Redwood will provide 30 days' notice prior to adding any new subprocessor used for transient routing unless a timeliness exception is required for critical security operations.
- Audit logs: Redwood will provide routing audit logs (redacted PII) for any failover event within 48 hours upon request; longer-term exports can be negotiated.

Next steps: if the above looks acceptable, I'll share the tracked DPA addendum. Rishi / Marissa — please confirm if offering the 30-minute contractual backstop requires any commercial adjustment for the pilot.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
